children: Investigators in California, who are probing whether Nvidia
unlawfully sold its advanced chips to China and misled investors, are also looking at whether the company engaged in potential criminal violations of state law. Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

The state’s top law enforcement officer, Attorney General Rob Bonta, announced an investigation into the California-based company on Thursday amid allegations that its advanced semiconductor chips found their way to China, breaching U.S. restrictions

“The basic legal framework that we’re looking at is the prohibitions in California law — both civil and criminal — against misleading investors and the public,” Bonta said in an interview, adding, “And there are multiple different laws that provide prohibitions in that space.”

is under public scrutiny after its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week amid reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including with a suspected Chinese spy that allegedly threatened U.S. national security.

Any potential finding by the California AG’s office that the company unlawfully sold chips to China and misled the public may ultimately have no connection with Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, Bonta said.

“It could be either or neither. That’s why we’re doing an investigation,” he added. “So there could be an affair that has nothing to do with selling chips to China — that’s something that Nvidia may have done on its own — or maybe it didn’t sell any chips to China, affair or not.”
is found to have breached the law, his office could seek a court order to prevent further violations and claw back any profit generated from illegal sales, which could be significant, Bonta said.

If any violations are found, the company runs the risk of facing a criminal case, which could lead to additional financial penalties, according to Bonta. “It could,” he said. “It depends on what was done, what the facts show, who knew what when, what the intent and state of mind was, and what the conduct was, but it could potentially.”

title: Nvidia probe in California extends to potential criminal violations: Bloomberg
